overview.text: The Black-headed Python is a non-venomous python of northern Australia, easily known by its shiny black head and neck.

identification.text: Glossy black head and neck; muscular, slightly flattened body; a tail that tapers to a thin point.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 1.5 to 2 m long, up to 3.5 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The northern half of Australia (Western Australia, Northern Territory, Queensland), away from the driest areas.

behaviour.text: Lives on the ground among rocks and debris. If disturbed it hisses loudly but rarely bites; it swims well but is almost never found in water.

diet.text: Mainly reptiles, especially skinks, but also geckos, bearded dragons, legless lizards, snakes and even large monitor lizards; sometimes mammals and birds.

reproduction.text: Lays 5 to 10 eggs and coils around them to keep them warm until they hatch.

recognise.text: Shiny black head and neck on a banded brown body.
